Detroit is a 3.5-point favorite in the latest Lions vs. Panthers odds from DraftKings Sportsbook, and the Over/Under on the game total is set at 47.5 points. Bet on Sunday Night Football at DraftKings, where new users get $150 in bonus bets after they spend $5+: One major downside for the Panthers is that they have been ravaged by injuries recently, including losing their best offensive lineman, Damien Lewis , for a while. They also placed both starting cornerbacks on IR, so things could be dicey against this explosive Lions offense. Get a $55 bonus after $25 in trades by claiming the latest Kalshi promo code CBSSPORTS55 here : Best bets for Sunday Night Football Over 51.5 This line has climbed a full point over the last 24 hours, and that probably involves the weather. It was supposed to dump rain all day Sunday in North Carolina, but we're now staring down just some chill in the air and what should be a fun one. The Lions' last appearance in prime time cashed everyone out with the explosive matchup against the Bills . I'm not expecting Carolina to perform like Buffalo did, but the Panthers are highly susceptible to being dragged into shootouts if their opponent starts to sling the ball around. Given the dearth of defensive backfield talent out there for Carolina, I fully expect the Lions to take advantage and throw the ball downfield. Carolina should be able to answer and we should get points galore. Sunday Night Football player props Darren Waller Over 36.5 receiving yards (-112, DraftKings) Bryce Young is going to be forced to pass the ball in this one, and that should bode well for Waller, who's been a surprisingly impressive target for the Panthers as a late addition to the roster. He broke out in Week 2 with a pair of scores then was rewarded with eight targets in Week 3 against the Browns . I'd expect him to see close to that many again Sunday night, making this number just way too low for how much Bryce looks his way, especially if Jalen Coker ends up inactive tonight. Jahmyr Gibbs Over 37.5 receiving yards (-115, DraftKings) Gibbs is the unquestioned best running back in football right now and has really rewarded anyone who took him first overall in fantasy. But he's not just a great runner, he's also an elite receiver, and in a game that should be a shootout with Jared Goff looking to exploit the Panthers defense, I'd expect Gibbs to be plenty involved in the pass game as well. 40 receiving yards feels very, very doable for the superstar. Bet on NFL player props and more at BetMGM: Sunday Night Football anytime touchdowns Jameson Williams (+200, DraftKings) If Williams wasn't having such a meh year so far, this number wouldn't be north of 2-1. But he's been just OK thus far, and as such we're getting a great price. Jamo can score from anywhere, should get plenty of short-yardage looks with screens and the like and also is the ultimate deep threat going against a really depleted secondary. Brycen Tremayne (+360, DraftKings) This is a bit of a longshot, but, again, we're thinking Jalen Coker won't play in this game. That's going to likely slide Tremayne into a starting role opposite of Tetairoa McMillan at wide receiver, and if this is a shootout, Young is going to have to throw a lot. There's a good chance Tremayne gets lost in the sauce near the end zone, setting him up as a nice high-value play to score. By Zachary Cohen - October 3, 2026 87572 X Facebook Email It’s time for Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season. I strongly suggest you check out the Week 4 NFL Betting Hub , where you’ll find all of the features and picks from my talented co-workers. On top of that, we never stop pumping out good NFL content on our live shows . That’s the beauty of being a subscriber. As a company, we’re relentless in our effort to get you prepared for these games. With that out of the way, let’s get into the fun stuff. Keep reading for my Week 4 NFL best bets and Week 4 NFL player props. MORE: Check out our Pro Picks page for NFL best bets from all of our analysts Indianapolis Colts vs. Washington Commanders – 9:30 am ET (London) The Colts might be down Alec Pierce, but I like the way this offense operates. Indianapolis lost a tough one in Kansas City two weeks ago, but the team put up 30 points against a Chiefs team that is sixth in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (-0.077) this year. It’s just hard to stop the Colts once Jonathan Taylor gets going on the ground. He puts Indianapolis in a ton of manageable third-and-short situations. Of course, Washington is a top-five team in Rush EPA/Play Allowed (-0.318) right now. The Commanders have done a good job of stuffing opponents thus far. But they haven’t seen an offensive line quite like this, and they haven’t faced a running back this efficient. Also, if Washington is selling out to stop the run, Daniel Jones should be able to do some real damage through the air — especially when looking Josh Downs’ way. I also happen to love the Commanders to put up points on the Colts defense. Marcus Mariota is an excellent backup, so Washington’s offense isn’t going to completely stall out with Jayden Daniels injured. Mariota played well in relief of Daniels two games ago, and he threw for three touchdowns in his start last week. He’s accurate, he understands the offense, and he’s still a threat with his legs. He’s also up against a Colts defense that is 30th in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (0.124). Honestly, this might not seem like the most enticing standalone game, but I think it’s going to deliver some early-morning excitement. Two shaky defenses should mean a real shot at a shootout. Also, since 2024, the Over is 15-1 when Washington is an underdog of 3.5 to 9.5 points. The average total points scored in such games is 58.2 points per game. Bet: Over 46.5 (-115) Dallas Cowboys at Houston Texans – 1:00 pm ET We haven’t seen anything from Houston this season, but a bounce-back performance should be coming soon. I don’t expect the Texans to completely stifle a good Cowboys offense, but I do know that Houston is much better than its No. 19 ranking in EPA/Play Allowed (0.012) this year. This is a Texans defense that has been elite for years, and none of the moves made in the offseason should have resulted in this type of drop-off. That said, look for Houston to start playing some much better defense, and we could see it start with a decent showing against Dak Prescott and Co. I also love any offense in a matchup with the Cowboys defense, as Dallas is at the bottom of the league in EPA/Play Allowed (0.193). The Cowboys made some moves to address their miserable defense from last season, but it doesn’t look like any of them have worked. So, this should be a pretty strong matchup for CJ Stroud. Of course, Stroud has issues as a passer, but he’s reliable when he has time to get his feet set. That’s a good thing as Stroud prepares to face a defense that is 31st in Pass Rush Win Rate (40%). He should have plenty of time. This is also a massive desperation spot for Houston. I can’t imagine Dallas is thrilled to be sitting at 1-2 right now, but Houston’s season might be over if the team drops this one to fall to 0-4. Bet: Texans ML (-136) Arizona Cardinals at New York Giants – 1:00 pm ET Jameis Winston has been pretty buttoned up since taking over for Jaxson Dart, but I imagine he’ll be slinging it around a bit here. This season, the Cardinals are allowing 247.0 passing yards per game, and their two starting corners have an average PFF grade of 52.1. New York has been conservative with Winston so far, opting to lean heavily into a ground-and-pound approach. However, the Giants need to play the matchup, and this is one that calls for some passing. Arizona is a top-10 team in pass frequency. So, if the Cardinals are letting Jacoby Brissett air it out, the Giants will have no choice but to let Winston do the same. I know Winston hasn’t yet thrown for a score, and he also hasn’t eclipsed 118 passing yards in a game. But we all know that Winston is a gunslinger, and you don’t have to go back too far to find a box score in which he threw for 366 yards and two touchdowns. That was November 23, 2025, when Winston got involved in a shootout with the Lions. Week 4 arrives with no shortage of NFL betting action, major storylines and roster shakeups, which means we're back with another look at the most notable angles from the weekly slate. Between prediction markets opening a new way of sports trading and sportsbooks ramping up the promos, NFL betting is at an all-time high this season and we are here to make sure you don't miss a beat as we head into Week 4. Find the narrative, check the data and let the numbers inside our NFL predictions do the rest while you sit back and take in every game this season. Below, we break down the week's biggest storylines, our model's top spread and moneyline picks, and the players, markets and scenarios most worth your attention. Three storylines to watch in Week 4 1. Sunday morning football from London Set your alarms! We've had two international games already this season, but they haven't messed with the broadcast schedule as Rams-Niners from Australia was our TNF game, and Cowboys-Ravens this past weekend was on in the Sunday afternoon window. Colts vs. Commanders will be the first overseas game with a Sunday morning kickoff, getting udnerway at 9:30 AM ET from Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. Both teams are coming off Week 3 wins and big improvements, with Washington unlocking the ceiling of their offense and the Colts defense finally showing up after giving up over 70 points through two games. Early predictions for the Dimers model give a slight lean to the over 46.5 at 51.2%, and a 63.0% win probability for Indianapolis. Both RBs, Jonathan Taylor (66,1%) and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (55.2%), have strong TD probabilities and the top WRs for both teams, Josh Downs and Terry McLaurin , project to clear 60 receiving yards. 2. First place up for grabs in AFC West Could the Raiders really go 4-0? Las Vegas has rolled to three wins early this season behind QB Kirk Cousins , and head coach Klint Kubiak . At +800, they're tied atop the AFC West standings with the Chiefs who are -125. Both teams face off in Week 4. In the Patrick Mahomes era (since 2018), the Raiders have 3 wins against the Chiefs. The Raiders are 4.5-point underdogs this week, with a 51.6% chance the Chiefs cover on the way to a win. But, the Dimers model predicts the Raiders to put up a fight; both TE Brock Bowers and RB Ashton Jeanty are over a 43% chance for a touchdown, the second and third-most likely players to score in the game. The key for Vegas will be containing Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker , who's projected for 87 rushing yards (third-most of the week) and a 53.6% TD probability, the latter of which does rank outside our top 10 RBs for the week. 3. Next man up: RB edition Week 2 was the QBs, but Week 3 saw multiple starting RBs go down with injury. Breece Hall (Jets), De'Von Achane (Dolphins) and Travis Etienne Jr. (Saints) all left their games and are et to miss varying degrees of time. Achane is out for the season with a torn ACL, while Etienne (hamstring) and Hall (quad) are more week-to-week. In Miami, Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright are behind Achane, but Wright is day-to-day with his own foot injury, and Gordon projects to lead the backfield with a 25.2% TD probability and 33.3 rushing yards. Braelon Allen is the next man up behind Hall, and after scoring in Week 2, projects for 54.8 rushing yards and a substantial 47.4% TD probability vs. the Bears. In New Orleans, the committee of veteran Alvin Kamara and career backup Kendre Miller will split duties, with Kamara projected to lead with 35.9 rushing yards, 15.1 receiving yards and a 32.7% TD probability. These signals are the first to look for when researching a weekly NFL slate, as it shows where our model has proven to be most accurate . Due to the launch of our brand-new NFL model, only props have Sweet Spots that have carried over from last season. Once we have enough bets in the bank, you'll find game lines here as well. Two takeaways heading into Week 4: our top market of Rushing Yards has ticked up another 2.2% since Week 3, and 2+ touchdowns have made their way into positive ROI over 100 bets dating back to last season. This week, there are over 20 players with an edge to score twice. Players to watch in Week 4 These are players who need to be on your radar, whether in fantasy leagues or for player prop betting. Last week, we looked at Christian Watson (scored for the third straight game), CeeDee Lamb (7 catches, 112 yards) and Derrick Henry (two touchdowns). 1. Derrick Henry (Ravens) Yeah, we're looking at Derrick Henry again. Why, you ask? He's playing his former franchise, the Titans for the first time. Tennessee is as bad as ever and have the 24th-ranked rushing defense this season, allowing 126.3 yards per game and 3 rushing touchdowns. King Henry has six rushing touchdowns this season and enters this game with the highest touchdown probability of a player yet this season at 71.1% and his 12.9% chance for 3 or more touchdowns is a full 2% higher than any other player. 2. Tetairoa McMillan (Panthers) Panthers WR Tetairoa "Tet" McMillan has yet to find the end zone this season, and is coming off his first disappointing game of the year, catching just 2 of 5 targets for 17 yards. After a 1,000-yard, 7-TD rookie season, expectations have been high for the second-year wideout, but he hasn't scored. In Week 4 vs. the Lions, Tet projects for the 9th-most receiving yards of the week at 70.1 and a 28.2% TD probability. No team in the NFL has given up more passing yards than the Detroit Lions at 979 , 104 more than the next team, and their 9 passing TDs are the second-most allowed. 3. David Montgomery (Texans) After a 3-TD Week 1 performance, David Montgomery looked like a league-winner in fantasy and a top betting target. He has 42 rushing yards and no scores since then. Fortunately, he has the cure for all production ailments on tap in Week 4, a matchup with the Cowboys defense. Dimers' top-projected running backs in Week 4. Already bottom-tier and now dealing with injuries, the Cowboys have given up the second-most rushing yards this season at 539 (over 100 more than Denver at third-most) and 3 rushing touchdowns. Montgomery's rushing projection is solid but modest, though 69.1 yards would be the highest for him this season, and the fourth-highest TD probability of the week at 63.7%, with a substantial 26.9% probability to score twice, higher than OPOY favorites Bojan Robinson and Jaxon Smith-Njigba. I'm looking at you, Texans and Chargers. There are also a few early contenders that I'm thinking might be pretenders. New York Giants, anyone? Here's where I'm putting my money in Week 5. Buccaneers @ Cowboys The Cowboys are once again a machine on offense, sitting near the top of the league by averaging over 30 points per game. I expect another big offensive performance Thursday night against the reeling Bucs. Hill's Pick: Cowboys Over 29.5 (-115) Eagles vs. Jaguars The Eagles are a complete mess offensively, and have key injuries to many of their best players. I don’t think that gets fixed overnight. Hill's Pick: Eagles Under 17.5 (-140) Bears @ Packers A genius. A wizard. Bears head coach Ben Johnson is worthy of all the accolades, winning three games this year with three different starting quarterbacks. That being said, being a road favorite at Lambeau with a backup quarterback has me looking at the Packers. Hill's Pick: Packers +1.5 (-110) Texans @ Titans It’s now or never for the Texans, who can ill afford another loss and an 0-5 start. I’ll go Over the total here considering the Texans look to be improved on offense while their intimidating defense has regressed significantly in 2026. Hill's Pick: Over 38.5 (-110) Bengals @ Dolphins The Dolphins are 0-4 but have been feisty and rather competitive the last couple of weeks against the Chiefs and Vikings. The heat in Miami is a tough obstacle for visitors this time of year. I like the home team to keep it close. Hill's Pick: Dolphins +7.5 (-110) Raiders @ Patriots The Patriots perhaps saved their season last week with a clutch win in Buffalo. They are 2-2 despite having the most turnovers in the NFL (12). The Raiders have 10 takeaways, also the most in the NFL. There is a lot of randomness when it comes to turnovers. I’ll back the Patriots here, who are due for some better turnover luck. Hill's Pick: Patriots -3.5 (-110) Vikings @ Saints The Vikings have issues on offense but do have an excellent kicker in Will Reichard. Reichard is 12-for-12 this year on field goals, averaging three makes per game. Against a shaky Saints defense, I expect him to make a couple of field goals. Hill's Pick: Will Reichard Over 1.5 Made FGs (-150) Browns @ Jets Browns rookie receiver KJ Concepción had a breakout game last week with five catches for 64 yards on eight targets. The week before, he had nine targets against the Panthers. His prop is set at 40.5 this week, which seems a bit low. Hill's Pick: KJ Concepción Over 40.5 Receiving Yards (-109) Colts @ Steelers The Colts are playing a road game immediately after traveling back from London last week. The Steelers are home off of extra rest after losing to the rival Browns last week. The rest/travel situation heavily favors the home team. Hill's Pick: Steelers -2.5 (-110) Giants @ Commanders The Giants have hung on for close home wins vs. a soft schedule to get to 3-1, but I’ll take them +3.5 this week against a Commanders team that will send injury-prone quarterback Jayden Daniels back onto the field, with perhaps a cumbersome brace on his left elbow. Hill's Pick: Giants +3.5 (-110) Broncos @ Chargers It hasn’t been pretty for the disappointing Chargers, but they battled in the last two weeks, losing one-score games at Buffalo and Seattle. Eventually, they will win a game, and it might not be this week, but getting 3.5 at home against an underwhelming Broncos team is too good to pass up. Hill's Pick: Chargers +3.5 (-110) Lions @ Cardinals The Lions are 4-0 on the Over this year. They are very good on offense but abysmal defensively. I’ll stick with their Overs until proven otherwise. Hill's Pick: Over 54.5 (-110) 49ers @ Seahawks These teams have not played this year, but they have met twice in 2026. Seattle won both of those games by a combined score of 54-9. I’ll take the Seahawks to win again. Hill's Pick: Seahawks -3 (-110) Ravens @ Falcons Last week, I suggested taking Falcons’ star back Bijan Robinson Over his rushing prop and it cashed easily. It’s not fun, but this week I’ll take a shot on the Under, as Robinson draws a solid Baltimore rush defense that is allowing under four yards per carry. Hill's Pick: Bijan Robinson Under 89.5 Rushing Yards (-110) Bills @ Rams An exciting game on Monday night, but there are whispers that Bills quarterback Josh Allen is battling a knee injury. Allen only ran for four yards last week, so with his prop set at 36.5, I’ll go Under. I’ll back the Patriots here, who are due for some better turnover luck. Hill's Pick: Patriots -3.5 (-110) The Vikings have issues on offense but do have an excellent kicker in Will Reichard. Reichard is 12-for-12 this year on field goals, averaging three makes per game. Against a shaky Saints defense, I expect him to make a couple of field goals. Hill's Pick: Will Reichard Over 1.5 Made FGs (-150) Browns rookie receiver KJ Concepción had a breakout game last week with five catches for 64 yards on eight targets. The week before, he had nine targets against the Panthers. His prop is set at 40.5 this week, which seems a bit low. Hill's Pick: KJ Concepción Over 40.5 Receiving Yards (-109)

The Giants have hung on for close home wins vs. a soft schedule to get to 3-1, but I’ll take them +3.5 this week against a Commanders team that will send injury-prone quarterback Jayden Daniels back onto the field, with perhaps a cumbersome brace on his left elbow. Hill's Pick: Giants +3.5 (-110) It hasn’t been pretty for the disappointing Chargers, but they battled in the last two weeks, losing one-score games at Buffalo and Seattle. Eventually, they will win a game, and it might not be this week, but getting 3.5 at home against an underwhelming Broncos team is too good to pass up. Hill's Pick: Chargers +3.5 (-110) The Lions are 4-0 on the Over this year. They are very good on offense but abysmal defensively. I’ll stick with their Overs until proven otherwise. Hill's Pick: Over 54.5 (-110) These teams have not played this year, but they have met twice in 2026.

Bears head coach Ben Johnson is worthy of all the accolades, winning three games this year with three different starting quarterbacks. That being said, being a road favorite at Lambeau with a backup quarterback has me looking at the Packers. Hill's Pick: Packers +1.5 (-110) It’s now or never for the Texans, who can ill afford another loss and an 0-5 start. I’ll go Over the total here considering the Texans look to be improved on offense while their intimidating defense has regressed significantly in 2026. Hill's Pick: Over 38.5 (-110) The Dolphins are 0-4 but have been feisty and rather competitive the last couple of weeks against the Chiefs and Vikings. The heat in Miami is a tough obstacle for visitors this time of year. I like the home team to keep it close. Hill's Pick: Dolphins +7.5 (-110) The Patriots perhaps saved their season last week with a clutch win in Buffalo.

What Are NFL Player Props? NFL player prop bets allow fans to wager on the likelihood that a football star will perform above or below expectations in a specific statistical category, or that they will achieve certain notable events during the game. Like any wager, greater risk means higher payout, so placing a wager on a struggling quarterback to throw for four touchdowns will return stronger odds than a wager on the reigning MVP who has been on a hot streak. Why Bet on NFL Player Props? Player prop bets add a layer of entertainment to your NFL experience. Unlike a head-to-head matchup where you might place your bet and check the score after the game is over, placing wagers on individual achievements and statistics gives you even more reason to watch the game and root for the player you bet on. With a wager on a statistical category, each time that player achieves you are a step closer to a profitable bet, which adds entertainment and excitement to your experience. Just as there are a variety of positions, ways to score, and statistics involved in an NFL game, there are a wide variety of player prop bet options. Whether it is a wager on a favorite player or in a statistical category you love to follow, there is likely a player prop category for every bettor. Most Common NFL Player Prop Bets With so many unique positions and statistics in NFL football, there is just as much variety in the player prop bets available. You can choose over/under bets on passing yards, rushing yards, passing touchdowns, interceptions, and total receptions, depending on your chosen player’s position. If you notice that a receiver with potential is +500 to score a touchdown and you believe he’s due for a breakout game you will profit if the receiver scores a TD. You can also choose head-to-head matchups—for example, you can wager that your favorite quarterback will throw for more passing yards than the quarterback he is matched against in a given week. An NFL player prop is a bet on how an individual player will perform in a game. Instead of betting on the winner, point spread, or total score, you're betting on a specific outcome or statistic for that player. Common NFL player props include: Passing yards, completions, attempts, and passing touchdowns (quarterbacks). Rushing yards and rushing attempts (running backs, quarterbacks, and other rushers). Receptions and receiving yards (wide receivers, tight ends, and running backs). Anytime, first, and multiple touchdown scorers (eligible offensive players and defenses/special teams). Most player props are offered as over/under bets. For example, a sportsbook might set a quarterback's passing yards at 245.5. You can bet the over if you think he'll finish with 246 or more, or the under if you think he'll finish with 245 or fewer. Touchdown scorer props work differently: you’re simply betting whether a player scores, with the odds reflecting the sportsbook's assessment of how likely that is.
